title: How much acid and water are in 240 mL of solution?
description: A science lab mixes acid and water in the ratio one to five, and a bottle holds two hundred forty millilitres of the solution. The amount is shared into six equal groups, the same way as the example in the book, to find the acid and the water.
teaching_notes: One idea: the terms added give the number of equal groups in the whole mixture. Watch for students who take the acid as one fifth of the whole instead of one sixth.

video_script.why: The child splits a mixture of known total into its two parts by the sharing method.
video_script.substitution: Add the terms to get the groups, divide the total by the groups, then multiply each term by one group.
video_script.anchor: a lab bottle holding two hundred forty millilitres of solution, with the acid and water to be found
video_script.payoff_line: the bottle has forty millilitres of acid and two hundred millilitres of water

final_answer.value: 40 mL of acid and 200 mL of water
final_answer.spoken: forty millilitres of acid and two hundred millilitres of water

maths_rules: acid 1 x 40 = 40 mL; water 5 x 40 = 200 mL
video_script.design: One idea: terms added give the groups, one group times each term gives each liquid. The bottle stays in the anchor band and the working goes on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='bottle'/>A science lab has a bottle with two hundred forty millilitres of solution.
<bookmark mark='ratio'/>The acid and water in it are in the ratio one to five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much acid and how much water are in the bottle?

beats.on_screen: the bottle holds still and the question mark glows

marks.stop: the question mark glows in the accent colour

beats.on_screen: 12 counters in a row split into 4 equal groups of 3, with the ratio 3 : 1 above and the groups 9 and 3 below

marks.groups: the counters split into 4 groups of 3
marks.parts: the parts 9 and 3 appear under the groups
marks.same: the bottle slides beside the counters

narration: <bookmark mark='example'/>The example in your book shared twelve counters in the ratio three to one.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Three plus one is four, so there are four equal groups of three.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>One part takes three groups and the other takes one, which makes nine and three.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We will find the acid and water the same way as the example in your book.

marks.given: the amount of solution and the ratio are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two hundred forty millilitres of solution with acid and water in the ratio one to five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the acid and the water

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much acid and how much water.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Step one, add the terms one and five to get six groups.
<bookmark mark='size'/>Divide two hundred forty by six, which gives forty millilitres in one group.

marks.acid: 1 × 40 = 40 mL is written for the acid
marks.water: 5 × 40 = 200 mL is written for the water

narration: <bookmark mark='acid'/>Step two, multiply each term by one group. The acid is one times forty, which is forty millilitres.
<bookmark mark='water'/>The water is five times forty, which is two hundred millilitres.

beats.on_screen: put the answers back: 40 + 200 = 240; 40 : 200 = 1 : 5 (divide both by 40)

marks.back: the words put the answers back in the question are written

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, put the answers back in the question.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Forty plus two hundred is two hundred forty, the whole solution.
<bookmark mark='ratio'/>Divide both by forty and we get one to five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 40 mL of acid and 200 mL of water
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The bottle has forty millilitres of acid and two hundred millilitres of water.
